text:
elena: quick heads-up — after the RBAC change to service-account `sdlc-scanner-sa` we started seeing a spike in premerge SAST failures. suspect permission error when the scanner tries to fetch keystore metadata :thinking:

michael: which failures? any stack traces?

elena: most are `403` when hitting keystore API; snippet from CI log:```2026-03-16T14:02:11Z scanner: GET /keystore/replica-meta -> 403 Forbidden (rolebinding missing: projects:ci-scanners:view)```

raj: that matches the RBAC rollout earlier today — I removed clusterrolebinding for `ci-scanners` to tighten perms and left a TODO for the Keystore read role. my bad.

sophia: ok — two things: (1) we need an emergency scoped grant for the scanner to unblock merges, (2) audit log entries so we can show scope of access during the rollback.

elena: for the emergency grant, prefer least-privilege: `keystore.read-metadata` on namespace `ci` only. can we do that as a short-lived rolebinding? :pray:

raj: yes I can create a namespaced RoleBinding with TTL. Planning: create Role `keystore-reader-ci`, bind to `sdlc-scanner-sa`, annotate with `redwood/justification:scanner-unblock-20260316` and `redwood/expires-at: 2026-03-16T16:30:00Z`.

michael: also add `auditlog:request_id` propagation so we can correlate CI run -> keystore request. Right now our keystore logs show `service=keystore` but not original CI run id.

raj: good call. keystore supports X-Request-Id header. I'll add a small wrapper in the scanner config to pass `CI_RUN_ID` as `X-Request-Id` for requests.

scan-bot: nightly-scan-2435 finished with 12 new findings (high:0, medium:4, low:8) — linking results: https://scans.company/2435

elena: unrelated scan noise — some of the medium findings are duplicates of previous blobs that failed to fetch metadata and therefore generated parsing errors. after RBAC fix we should re-run those to confirm true positives.

sophia: can ops generate a retest job that replays the last 12 artifacts once the rolebinding is in place? prefer a single-run rebuild against exact commit SHA.

raj: can do. plan: (1) apply RoleBinding, (2) patch scanner env to forward CI_RUN_ID, (3) trigger `retest/1765873200` job pointing at sha `f9a3c2b`. ETA 15m.

michael: while you're doing that, I'm going to open a short RFC to formalize keystore client contract: headers required, expected error codes, and audit fields. we should document `keystore.read-metadata` and the minimum set of claims for SA token.

elena: thanks. after retest we'll validate findings and close duplicates. if any real vuln surfaces from metadata parsing, we'll triage ASAP. tagging @security-oncall

sophia: small follow-up — we should ensure the RoleBinding changes show up in our tamper-proof audit: send a copy of the applied k8s manifest to the keystore audit pipeline and kink to the ticket.

raj: done — applied manifest and added annotation `audit:uploaded-to-keystore-audit`. pushed retest job. logs:```kubectl apply -f rolebinding-scanner-ci.yaml -> rolebinding.rbac.authorization.k8s.io/scanner-keystore-reader created```

scan-bot: re-run `retest/1765873200` started (job id 1765873245)

elena: seeing first retest logs — scanner can fetch metadata again, no 403s. sample:```2026-03-16T14:21:03Z scanner: GET /keystore/replica-meta -> 200 OK (request_id=ci-1765873245)```

michael: good. can we please add a quick unit test in the scanner repo asserting `X-Request-Id` header presence so future RBAC changes don't silently break auditability?

raj: will do a tiny PR with test + docs.

elena: final note: we should run a phased review to identify any other service accounts that lost keystore read access during the RBAC tightening. I'll open a follow-up thread for a service-account inventory and map to required keystore roles. thanks everyone :thumbsup:
